{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that allowing learners to control the allocation of study time across items would result in higher recognition performance compared to a control condition where total study time was equated but items were presented for a fixed duration.",
  "design": "mixed",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Self-paced study (participants chose how long to study each word) versus fixed-rate study (participants were yoked to the total study time of a self-paced partner, with time distributed equally across items).",
  "outcome_measure": "Recognition memory performance measured by discriminability (da) using a 4-point confidence scale.",
  "population_and_setting": "Introductory-level psychology students at the University of Illinois, tested individually on desktop computers.",
  "sample_size_total": 148,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Students participated in exchange for course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "Comparison of mean discriminability (da) between self-paced and yoked fixed-rate conditions using t-tests, and an item analysis comparing discriminability calculated from the combined responses of each group.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were yoked in pairs; the first participant was assigned to the self-paced condition, and the second was assigned to the fixed-rate condition. Four primacy and four recency buffer words were excluded from analysis."
